content:
Brad Pitt already has his next dream role in mind — and it involves one of the most iconic film series of all time.

At the Los Angeles premiere of his new Netflix movie “The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth” on Monday, the Oscar winner revealed he would be down to star opposite Robert Pattinson’s Agent 007.

Pitt shared his desires to tackle the role after hearing on the red carpet that Amazon MGM selected the “Twilight” alum as the next James Bond.

“You know, I’d like to do that,” he told Extra TV. “My man Javier [Bardem] did it so well. It’s tall shoes, but I’d take that on.”

Pitt’s “F1” co-star Bardem starred as the cyberterrorist villain, Raoul Silva, in the 2012 James Bond film “Skyfall” opposite Daniel Craig, who starred as the fictional British Secret Service agent from 2006 to 2021.

Pitt gushed about Pattinson’s casting.

“I love this idea,” Pitt shared. “I love what he’s been doing. I love his choices, and I think he’s the real deal. That’s great. Good call.”

Pattinson was officially unveiled as the next Bond on Monday after rumors briefly circulated he was in the running to take on the titular role. The announcement came after years of speculation that actors Nicholas Hoult, Idris Elba, Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Aaron Taylor-Johnson and Josh O’Connor were being considered for the role.

Pitt isn’t the only star who is vying to be the next James Bond villain.

Hours after Pattinson’s new role was announced, his “Dune: Part Three” co-star, Florence Pugh, positioned herself as a possible antagonist to oppose the new 007.

“I sent [‘Dune’ director] Denis [Villeneuve] a message this morning, and I said, ‘Congratulations on finding a new Bond. Nice catch. Any villains with the size of 5’4’’?” she said at ELLE’s Women in Hollywood event in Beverly Hills, California, on Nov. 16 while being honored onstage.

Pugh added, “Anyway, I’m reminding you just in case!”

The next James Bond movie does not yet have a release date. No additional casting details have been announced yet.
